## What it is

Gitea is a self-hosted Git forge: repositories, issues, pull requests, packages and CI (Gitea Actions) ([go-gitea/gitea](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea)).

**Licence:** `MIT` (GitHub licence API; license-matrix row "Gitea"). Market class **L1**.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): developer: git, ci. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`), one container, from the upstream **rootless** image `gitea/gitea:28.3.0-rootless` (USER 1000:1000), not the default root image.
- Service: 3000 (web and Git over HTTP) and 2222 (Gitea's built-in SSH server).
- Volume: `gitea-data` (10 GiB) as two subPaths: `data/` at `/var/lib/gitea` and `config/` at `/etc/gitea` (`app.ini`). An init container creates both as UID 1000.
- Probes: `GET /api/healthz`.

## First run

Source: [docs.gitea.com](https://docs.gitea.com/installation/install-with-docker-rootless) "Installation with Docker (rootless)".

1. Install Gitea from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-gitea`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:3000:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-gitea port-forward svc/gitea 3000:3000
   ```
3. The install page appears. Keep SQLite (the database is then on the volume), set the site URL, and create the administrator account in "Administrator account settings". Until then **anyone who can reach the page can complete the installation**, so do it right after install.

## Not done yet

- SSH (2222) is reachable only inside the cluster.
- Gitea Actions runners are not packaged.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: it has not been tested against this image.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices where upstream gives none; they are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212765046, job `gate (gitea)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/gitea/gitea:28.3.0-rootless`: CRITICAL CVE-2026-123158 in `openssh-keygen` 10.3_p1-r1, fixed in 10.3_p1-r2. A CRITICAL with a fix fails the gate (§9.4 check 3).
- Passed: licence MIT matches, ClamAV (0 infected, amd64 and arm64), smoke test (GET / returned 200). Not signed with cosign (recorded as unsigned, informational).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.

**Hold (apps/market-unblock-2, 2026-11-13):** CRITICAL CVE-2026-123158 in `openssh-keygen` 10.3_p1-r1 (fixed in r2). `28.3.0-rootless` is the newest tag. Unblock: a rebuild on a newer Alpine. The registry was re-read on 2026-11-13: the pinned digest is unchanged and no newer fixed tag exists, so nothing is bumped (the gate was not weakened and the tier was not edited). It unblocks when the weekly `apps-rescan` or a manual `apps-gate-all` run computes a pass on a rebuilt image. No upstream issue link was looked up (the GitHub API is not reachable from the worker).
